Her household shows scarcity management through prioritizing rent, utilities, diapers, food, and pediatric care while delaying optional expenses (Q56-Q64, Q81). Future-oriented hopes focus on stability, education, and giving Hattie more options than constraints (Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: Hattie has no personal civic identity or voting behavior because she is one year old (Q23, Q95). Her household context is Democratic-leaning, shaped by concerns about childcare, health care, racial fairness, food prices, and safe neighborhoods (Q24-Q30, Q96). summaries.psychologist: Hattie presents as curious but fretful: she explores objects hands-on, especially blocks, then retreats or clings when overstimulated by loud sounds or unfamiliar situations (Q01, Q16, Q43-Q45). Her emotional regulation depends on attachment figures, music, quiet spaces, naps, and predictable routines (Q17, Q37, Q44).
